entry.title: CompScan: Your computer's health doctor. Fully local, private, free (Rust)
entry.summary:
I built CompScan: a fully local system health tool that scans your machine, finds what's slowing you down, spots security issues, and fixes things with one command. Nothing ever leaves your computer. Most "optimization" tools are either cloud-heavy, full of telemetry, or one-off scripts. I wanted one CLI that's private, cross-platform, and actually useful for developers. Health check: CPU/RAM hogs, disk space, caches (often 2-15 GB reclaimable) Security: SSH keys, credentials, firewall, permissions. Score out of 100. Habits: late-night usage, marathon sessions, suggests breaks One-click actions: cleanup caches, temp files, logs (trust-level gated) Rust, ~3 MB binary, redb for storage, optional Ollama for deeper reasoning. macOS, Linux, Windows. curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvk147/comp-scan/main/install.sh | bash
Or: cargo install --path . from the repo. If you care about privacy and a fast machine, give it a try: github.com/vvk147/comp-scan

entry.summary:
Every developer eventually encounters the infamous error: Access to fetch at 'https://api.example.com' from origin 'https://myapp.com' has been blocked by CORS policy
At first glance, it feels like the server blocked your request. But here’s the twist: The request was not blocked. refused to let your JavaScript read the response. Understanding this single idea makes CORS far less mysterious. Let's break it down step by step. 🟦 1. What is CORS? CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) is a browser-enforced security rule. It controls whether JavaScript running in the browser is allowed to read a response coming from another origin. Important truths: 🚨 CORS is not a server security system
